mystery that has intrigued Norway for nearly 50 years.</b></p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">In November 1970, the badly burnt body of a woman was found in a remote spot in Norway's Isdalen valley. </p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Someone had cut the labels off her clothes, and scraped distinctive marks off her belongings - as if to stop her from being identified.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">And as police started investigating her death, they uncovered a trail of coded messages, disguises, and fake identities - but never cracked the case.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Forty-six years later, Norwegian police and <a href="https://www.nrk.no/dokumentar/do-you-remember-this-woman_-1.13215629" class="ssrcss-1e0jzsh-InlineLink e1kn3p7n0">NRK journalists<span class="visually-hidden ssrcss-i2z2ig-VisuallyHidden e16en2lz0">, <!-- -->external</span></a> have decided to reopen the investigation.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">This is the story of the Isdal Woman - and the perplexing trail of clues she left behind.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">But the woman does not appear to be a normal hiker.</p></div></div></div></div></div><div class="ssrcss-8ppqmm-Wrap e42f8511"><div data-block="image" to mimic her style. In fact, I remember her winking at me… from my perspective it felt as though she thought I had been staring a bit too much at her."</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"On one occasion There weren't too many foreign tourists in Bergen then - and the fact the woman seemed wealthy, and well-travelled, sparked a lot of speculation.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"This was during the Cold War, and there were definitely a lot of spies in Norway, including Russian spies," says Gunnar Staalesen, a Bergen-based crime author who was a university student at the time.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">There were also Israeli agents operating in Norway - as shown three years later, when Mossad agents killed a man in Lillehammer they had mistaken for a terrorist, he adds.</p></div></div></div></div></div><div class="ssrcss-8ppqmm-Wrap e42f8511"><div data-block="image" class="ssrcss-bcrzx2-ComponentWrapper e1aon0op1"><div class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">But after investigative journalists at NRK make queries about the Isdal Woman, Prof Morild finds the jaw - deep in a cellar in Haukeland University Hospital's forensic archives. </p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">The find gives Norwegian police the opportunity to re-open the case, and use the latest forensic techniques to try and identify the woman.</p></div></div></div></div></div><div class="ssrcss-8ppqmm-Wrap e42f8511"><div data-block="image" class="ssrcss-bcrzx2-ComponentWrapper e1aon0op1"><div class="ssrcss-126h8e-Spacer e5tfeyi1"><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">The Norwegian Criminal Investigation Service (Kripos) and University of Bergen start conducting isotope analysis on her teeth - looking at the chemical "signature" left by the elements that made up her teeth as they were being formed. </p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">The tests involve:</p><div class="ssrcss-2st5ed-ListContainer e5tfeyi0"><ul role="list"><li><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Oxygen isotope analysis, which can reveal the type of water the woman drank as she grew up - and which areas the water came from.</p></li><li><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Strontium isotope analysis, which can reflect the types of food the woman ate, and the type of soil in the area where she grew up.</p></li></ul></div><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">It's the first time Norwegian police have conducted isotope analysis on teeth - but they hope the findings will help them pinpoint the region where the woman lived.</p></div></div></div></div></div><div class="ssrcss-8ppqmm-Wrap e42f8511"><div data-block="subheadline" class="ssrcss-1sc9t00-Heading e10rt3ze0"><span role="text">Clue nine: The tissue samples</span></h2></div></div></div></div><div class="ssrcss-8ppqmm-Wrap e42f8511"><div data-block="text" class="ssrcss-1sp09lk-ComponentWrapper e1aon0op1"><div class="ssrcss-126h8e-Spacer e1aon0op0"><div data-testid="rich-text"><div class="ssrcss-nqezkk-RichTextContainer e5tfeyi1"><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">DNA analysis is now one of the key tools police use in forensic analysis and identification cases.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">It didn't exist back in 1970.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">But it turns out several tissue samples from the woman's organs, including from her lungs, heart, adrenal gland and ovaries, have been stored at Haukeland University Hospital.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Prof Morild says it "has been a custom in most of Norway" to keep tissue samples from post mortem examinations. The samples are "useful for repeat examinations, and as a source of DNA".</p></div></div></div></div></div><div class="ssrcss-8ppqmm-Wrap e42f8511"><div data-block="image" class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">After months of work, scientists have an extended DNA profile of the woman. The latest results, published on Friday, show the woman was of European descent - making the theory that the woman was an agent from Israel much less likely.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Norwegian police are set to issue an Interpol black notice - which seeks information on unidentified bodies - with the new information.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">European police forces will be asked to check their DNA databases to see if they find a match. </p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"If someone in her close family is in a DNA registry somewhere, we will get a hit," says Ståle Hansen. "That would be really exciting."</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">The Isdal Woman case has been unsolved for the last 46 years. But now, modern science has reopened the possibility of this elusive Nordic mystery being solved. </p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10"><i>Readers who recognise the Isdal Woman or want to share tips about the case of the Isdal Woman can </i><a href="https://www.nrk.no/dokumentar/do-you-remember-this-woman_-1.13215629" class="ssrcss-1e0jzsh-InlineLink e1kn3p7n0">contact the NRK
